tZh: AI 科学家已至：自主实验室与合成超级智能——Periodic Labs
sEn: Liam of Periodic Labs explains why intelligence alone is insufficient and how autonomous physical laboratories close the loop between hypothesis and reality.
sZh: Periodic Labs 的 Liam 阐释为何仅有智能还不够，以及自主物理实验室如何闭合假设与现实之间的循环。

consensus.en: Intelligence is necessary but insufficient; new knowledge arises when ideas are tested against reality.
consensus.zh: 智能是必要条件但非充分条件；只有当想法与现实相碰撞时，新知识才会产生。

consensus.en: Scientific discovery by definition lies outside training data, so AI must run real experiments.
consensus.zh: 科学发现按定义就在训练数据之外，因此 AI 必须进行真实实验。

consensus.en: Materials science is harder than math or coding because of noise, uncertainty, and missing context.
consensus.zh: 材料科学比数学或编程更难，因为存在噪声、不确定性和上下文缺失。

consensus.en: Automated characterization is the biggest bottleneck; closing the loop through simulations is key.
consensus.zh: 自动化表征是最大的瓶颈；通过模拟闭环是关键。

consensus.en: High-quality, low-noise experimental data is more valuable than extra compute for physical discovery.
consensus.zh: 对于物理发现，高质量、低噪声的实验数据比额外算力更有价值。

consensus.en: Multidisciplinary teams of theorists, experimentalists, and AI researchers are essential for progress.
consensus.zh: 理论家、实验家和 AI 研究者组成的多学科团队对取得进展至关重要。

contrarian.en: Even a perfect frontier model will still need experiments to discover new materials.
contrarian.zh: 即使是最完美的前沿模型，也仍然需要实验来发现新材料。

contrarian.en: Humanoid robots would slow down lab automation compared to pragmatic, task-specific automation.
contrarian.zh: 相比务实的、针对特定任务的自动化，人形机器人反而会拖慢实验室自动化。

contrarian.en: Quantum computers won't help materials discovery much if we still model perfect crystals.
contrarian.zh: 如果我们仍然只模拟完美晶体，量子计算机对材料发现的帮助不会很大。

contrarian.en: Negative results and failed synthesis attempts are valuable training data, not waste.
contrarian.zh: 负面结果和失败的合成尝试是有价值的训练数据，而非浪费。

contrarian.en: Scaling laws alone won't solve science; physical experiments are irreplaceable.
contrarian.zh: 仅靠缩放定律无法解决科学问题；物理实验不可替代。

contrarian.en: The best AI researchers should work hands-on in labs, not just manage from afar.
contrarian.zh: 最优秀的 AI 研究者应该亲自动手在实验室工作，而不仅仅是在远处管理。

turns.en: This is another point. I talked to many biologist friends, and they are always very surprised when you say that in materials science you cannot just do XRD structure and find out what it actually is. turns.en: It's hard not to give up, crazy, responding to this question. But isn't it? turns.zh: 很难不放弃，疯狂地回应这个问题。但难道不是吗？在你看来，有机化学和生物学几乎来自一个 VC 维更低的模型，也就是按柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂度更低？我们似乎能把它表示成一维序列，几乎可以编译。所以，关键在于按柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂度更容易看出复杂性。一维？我是说 DNA 或 RNA——它只是序列。大多数人会说这更像是二维的，但我不是生物学家，所以我不确定他们是对的。

And the way atoms interact with each other is strange. For example, covalent bonds, ionic bonds, metallic bonds.
turns.zh: 但在无机化学里，一切都是化学，否则就只是疯狂。这显然不是来自低柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂度的模型，因为这些三维无机晶体可能包含金属、绝缘体、超导体、金刚石。这都是真的吗？差异大得难以置信。人们尝试过，但我们从未找到一维表示。例如，很难为三维无机晶体找到 SMILES 字符串。原子之间相互作用的方式很奇怪。例如，共价键、离子键、金属键。

turns.en: But yes, that's very interesting. I sometimes wonder—have you ever studied problems with solid electrolytes? Why can't people replace liquid electrolytes in batteries with solid? All are formed there—these dendrites. Essentially, lithium forms structures that penetrate into the solid electrolyte and destroy it. You look at this and how much do you think it is primitive compared with biology? After all, in biology these systems are capable of such complex nanotechnological progress. While we cannot even force two interfaces to work together, because everything breaks. Although, probably, inorganic materials can be very resistant to high temperatures. With them they can build space shuttles. Can use silicon for calculations according to Moore's law. So yes, this is a compromise.
turns.zh: 但是的，这非常有趣。我有时会想——你研究过固态电解质的问题吗？为什么人们不能用固态电解质替代电池中的液态电解质？那里形成的都是这些枝晶。本质上，锂形成结构，穿透固态电解质并破坏它。你看这个，你觉得与生物学相比它有多原始？毕竟，在生物学中这些系统能够实现如此复杂的纳米技术进展。而我们甚至无法让两个界面协同工作，因为一切都会断裂。尽管无机材料可能非常耐高温。用它们可以建造航天飞机。可以用硅进行计算，遵循摩尔定律。所以是的，这是一种妥协。

turns.en: Yes, we discussed this with a few other guests.
